h1: Concrete Driveway Contractor Serving London, Ontario

sectionTitle: What London's neighbourhoods mean for your driveway

blocks.text: London's clay soil and why your base matters

Most of London sits on heavy clay subsoil left behind by the glacial till that covers this part of Southwestern Ontario. Clay holds water, expands when it freezes, and shrinks when it dries out over the summer. If a driveway is poured on a thin or poorly compacted gravel base, that clay movement is what causes the heaving, cracking and settling you see on older driveways around the city. Before we form anything, we excavate down past the topsoil and organic layer, then place and compact a granular base thick enough to give the slab something stable to sit on, regardless of what the clay underneath is doing.

The frost line in London runs to roughly 1.2 metres, which is why footings for attached structures need to go deep, but a driveway slab itself doesn't need to be footed that far down — it needs a well-drained, well-compacted base and enough reinforcement to move as one piece rather than cracking into pieces. We reinforce every driveway with rebar or wire mesh sized to the slab, not a one-size-fits-all sheet, and we cut control joints at intervals that let the concrete crack where we want it to, not where it wants to.

A lot of what we do in neighbourhoods like Old North, Old South, Wortley Village and parts of Oakridge is driveway replacement rather than new installation. Homes built from the 1950s through the 1970s in these areas often have narrow, single-car driveways poured with less reinforcement and a thinner base than current practice calls for. When we replace one of these, we typically remove and dispose of the old slab, re-excavate to proper depth, and often widen the drive to fit two vehicles side by side — something we handle regularly as part of our /concrete-driveways work.

In newer subdivisions around Summerside, Hyde Park, Riverbend and parts of Lambeth, the driveways are usually newer builder-grade concrete. These tend to fail differently — often from a base that wasn't compacted properly during construction, or control joints that were spaced too far apart. We see the same diagonal cracking pattern often enough in these subdivisions that it's become a familiar call: a driveway five to ten years old, still under the original pour, already showing stress cracks running corner to corner.
Driveway widening and City of London permit rules

Widening a driveway in London means extending the paved or concrete surface, sometimes closer to a property line or over part of the boulevard. The City of London has specific rules about how close a driveway can come to a property line, how wide it can be relative to the garage or house, and how it needs to meet the boulevard and curb. Curb cuts for a widened driveway may require a separate application, and setbacks vary by zoning designation, so we check the applicable requirements for your property before we quote a widening project. This keeps the finished driveway compliant and avoids a costly redo.

Neighbourhoods like Byron and Westmount, with their mature trees and established lots, sometimes have additional root systems and mature landscaping to work around during excavation. We flag these site conditions during your free estimate so there are no surprises once the crew is on-site and forms are going in.
Driveway finishes London homeowners ask for most

items: Standard broom finish — the most common, cost-effective choice at $10–$16 per square foot, giving a slip-resistant texture that holds up under road salt and snow clearing
Exposed aggregate — popular in Masonville and Byron for its upscale look and strong traction
Stamped concrete driveways — cobblestone and brick patterns are the most requested stamps in London, typically $15–$25 per square foot
Integral colour and acid stain — used to match brick or stone accents on newer builds in Hyde Park and Riverbend

blocks.text: Whatever finish you choose, London Concrete Forming builds every driveway to handle our region's freeze-thaw cycles and winter road salt exposure, which is one of the harder tests a residential concrete surface faces in Ontario. We recommend a proper cure period of 7 days before vehicle traffic and a sealer application in the following season to extend the surface life, especially on stamped and coloured driveways.
Considering a wider driveway or a full replacement? Read our guide on the /blog/advantages-of-a-concrete-driveway before your free estimate — it covers the questions London homeowners ask most.
Scheduling and timeline for a London driveway

Most standard driveway jobs in London take two to three days on-site: one day for excavation, base preparation and forming, a second day for the pour and finish, and occasionally a third day if weather or drying conditions require it. After the pour, plan for a full 7-day cure before parking vehicles on the new surface. We schedule London projects with the shortest lead times in our service area, and free on-site estimates are typically booked within 2 to 5 business days of your call.

If your project also touches a walkway, a patio near the front entrance, or a stamped concrete driveway paired with matching steps, London Concrete Forming can coordinate the whole scope in a single visit and a single written quote, rather than splitting it across separate contractors.

faqs.q: Can you widen my existing London driveway without repouring the whole thing?
faqs.a: In most cases we recommend removing and repouring the full slab when widening, since tying new concrete to an old edge rarely holds up under freeze-thaw movement. We will assess your specific driveway during the free estimate and explain the most durable option for your property.

faqs.q: Do you need to pull a permit for a driveway replacement in London?
faqs.a: A like-for-like driveway replacement generally does not require a permit, but widening a driveway or changing a curb cut typically does under City of London rules. We confirm what applies to your address before quoting.

faqs.q: How do you handle mature trees and landscaping near older London driveways?
faqs.a: We assess root systems and landscaping during the on-site estimate in neighbourhoods like Byron and Westmount, and we plan excavation to minimize root damage wherever possible while still reaching proper base depth.

faqs.q: Is stamped concrete a good fit for London's winters?
faqs.a: Yes, provided it is properly sealed and reinforced. We build every stamped driveway with the same base preparation and reinforcement as a standard driveway, then recommend re-sealing every two to three years to protect the pattern and colour against road salt.
